features.title: Pay, spending and transfers, month by month
features.body: Plan's monthly savings now only averages months that every account you use has history for, so a bank that sent less history no longer looks like months with no pay. Money moved between your own accounts and card payments is left out, and a paycheck that landed uncategorized still counts as pay once a pay stub matches it. Tap See each month under the slider to check pay, other money in, spending and transfers for every month.

title: Back takes you back to where you were

features.title: Back keeps your place
features.body: Open a holding from far down Portfolio, go back, and you land on the same spot with your search, sort, filters and open rows as you left them. Home, Spending, Budget, Plan and Settings keep their place too, whether you use the back link at the top, the back button or a swipe. Tapping a tab still opens the page fresh.

features.title: Saving a month, line by line
features.body: Plan now starts from the pay that actually lands in your accounts, adds what your pay stubs say goes into your 401(k), HSA or ESPP, and takes off your spending. Under the slider you can see each line and how they add up. One unusual pay stub, like a bonus, no longer moves the number.

title: One row per investment, and a nudge when prices dip

features.title: The same fund in several accounts shows once
features.body: Portfolio holdings now show each investment once with its total. Tap one marked with a number of accounts to see how much sits in each, with shares and gain. Prefer to see each account on its own? Switch to By account.

features.title: Dip alerts
features.body: Get a note on your phone when anything you hold falls 10% under its 52-week high (and again at 20%, 30%), or drops under its 200-day average. They're facts about the price, not advice. Change them or add your own in Settings, Alerts.

features.title: 50- and 200-day averages
features.body: A holding's Key numbers now show its 50- and 200-day averages and how far today's price is above or under each.

features.title: Search and filter spending
features.body: Spending has a search box and a Filters button. Search by merchant, then narrow by category, account, money in or out, amount, and dates from this month to your whole history. The totals at the top add up everything that matches.

features.title: See what's behind a budget line
features.body: Tap a budget line and choose See this month's transactions to open Spending already filtered to that category.

features.title: Search and sort holdings
features.body: Portfolio holdings can be searched by ticker or name, sorted by size, today's move or total gain, and narrowed to one account or kind of holding. Your real exposure has a box to find any company, so you can see how much Apple you really own.

title: A plan that starts from your own numbers

features.title: Every plan number, worked out for you
features.body: Monthly savings now comes from your pay stubs (take-home plus 401(k) and HSA) against a typical month of spending, even with only one recent stub; the market return comes from your own mix of stocks, bonds and cash; and spending later comes from your real transactions. Each slider says where its number came from, and "Use it" takes you back after a what-if.

title: A heads-up before a budget goes over

features.title: Where the month is heading
features.body: Each budget line now says where it's heading by month-end, like "on track to spend $520, $70 over". Bills that haven't come yet are counted once at their usual amount; everyday spending follows this month's pace. When a category is on pace to go over, your phone gets a heads-up, once a month per category, with no amounts on the lock screen.

features.title: Know when there's a new version
features.body: A small card tells you when a new version is out, with what's in it, and Settings shows the version you're on and when it last looked. Tap Not now and it waits for the next one.

features.title: Update now, safely
features.body: The owner can install a new version from the app. The server still does the work: it checks the new version's signature, backs up first, and goes back on its own if the new version doesn't start cleanly. The app never gets any control over the server.

features.title: Draft with AI
features.body: Budget has a Draft with AI button. It looks at your spending by month, the lines you changed by hand, your pay stubs and your savings goal, then suggests a limit for each line with the reason. Only totals are sent, and you see exactly what first. Tick the ones you want; the old budget stays in History.

features.title: A morning brief
features.body: A few lines each morning: safe to spend, yesterday's spending, anything over budget, net worth and big moves. Your phone just says it's ready, with no amounts on the lock screen. Turn it on in Settings, Alerts. With AI set up, AI words it, checked against your own numbers.

features.title: Ask your own AI
features.body: Settings, Agents gives Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor a read-only key, so you can ask things like "how much did we spend on dining this year?" Agents can look but never change anything, and a key can be revoked at any time.

title: Your plan, and a guide to get set up

features.title: When work becomes optional
features.body: Plan now shows the year your savings could cover your spending, as a range from 4% to 8% returns after inflation, on a chart that runs from your net worth so far into the future. Drag across it to read any year, and add your birth year to see it as an age.

features.title: What if you saved more, or spent less?
features.body: Move the sliders for monthly savings, spending later (lean, regular or comfortable, made from your own budget), market returns and the withdrawal rate, and the date moves as you drag. Save the one you like as your plan.

features.title: Ways to save more
features.body: Plan lists the subscriptions you pay every month, flags the ones whose price went up, shows how much sooner you'd get there without them, and points out categories creeping up on their usual month. Worked out on your server, no AI.

features.title: A guide to get set up
features.body: A short checklist takes you from the first sign-in to a working app: Face ID, accounts, the budget, a test alert, then the extras. Each step ticks itself off. It sits on Home until you're done, and in Settings after.

title: Live prices, alerts and what's really inside your funds

features.title: Live prices and a page for every holding
features.body: Holdings update every 15 minutes while markets are open. Tap any holding for its price chart (drag across it to read any day), the day's and year's range, dividend yield, your shares across accounts and what you've gained.

features.title: Your real share of every company
features.body: Portfolio now looks inside your funds, using each fund's SEC filing, so Apple held directly and Apple inside your index funds add up to one number. A map shows funds and companies; tap a bubble to see where it comes from.

features.title: Alerts that know when to stay quiet
features.body: Get a push when a price crosses a line, a budget gets close, or one company grows past 10% of your portfolio. Each alert is sent once, and overnight ones wait until morning as a single message. Set them up in Settings → Alerts.

features.title: Bring your own AI
features.body: Settings, AI takes Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or a server on your own network like Ollama. Keys are encrypted, nothing is sent until you turn a provider on, and a monthly cap keeps the cost in check.

features.title: Upload any statement
features.body: Excel files, PDF statements, scanned pay stubs and screenshots now work too. When the built-in readers don't know a file, the app shows exactly what AI would see, with names and account numbers taken out, and asks first. Nothing is saved until you check it.

features.title: A budget that drafts itself
features.body: Budget starts with a draft built from your last few months: what each bill and everyday category usually costs, with a little room on everyday spending. Tap any line to change it. Every save is kept, so you can bring an older budget back.

features.title: Your true savings rate
features.body: Add a pay stub (five numbers, filled in from the last one) and the savings rate counts 401(k), HSA and ESPP money taken out before payday. Without a stub it works from take-home pay. Employer match is a switch.

features.title: Safe to spend and an emergency fund
features.body: Home shows what's left of the everyday budget for the rest of the month. Budget shows how many months of essentials your cash covers, against a target you pick.

features.title: Sign in with a glance
features.body: Set up with the code from the server, add a code app as the backup, then a passkey so Face ID or your fingerprint is all it takes. Invite your partner from Settings, People. Settings, Security shows every device that's signed in and everything that happened.

features.title: Link accounts or upload a file
features.body: Connect banks and cards through Plaid and brokerages through SnapTrade, all read-only, or upload a CSV or OFX file from Fidelity, E*TRADE or your bank. Everything syncs every few hours, and you'll get a push if a connection stops.

features.title: Spending that sorts itself
features.body: Transfers between your own accounts and card payments are left out. Merchants are cleaned up and categorized; fix one in two taps and the app remembers for next time.

features.title: The app, ready to install on your phone
features.body: Open the app on your phone and add it to your home screen. Home shows net worth with today's change, what's safe to spend for the rest of the month, the three budgets closest to their limit and your latest alerts. Spending, Budget, Portfolio and Plan are one tap away in the bar at the bottom. The eye button blurs every amount when someone is looking over your shoulder. This release runs on sample data; linking your own accounts comes with sign-in in the next phase.
